title: Jacob Gedleyihlekisa Zuma - South Africa: Overcoming Apartheid
content: ANC leader and Deputy President of South Africa. His middle name was part of a sentence his father constructed – “Ngeke ngithule umuntu engigedla engihlekisa”, which means “I can’t keep quiet when someone pretends to love me with a deceitful smile.” The last part of the sentence was given to Zuma as a name, while the first part became the name of his brother, Ngekengithule. In 1977 he became a member of the ANC’s Executive Committee. In the 1980s he was a member of the ANC’s political and military council. A Zulu himself, he was seen as the ideal person to negotiate with the IFP and to get support for the ANC in Natal. In 1991, at the first ANC National Conference in South Africa after the organisation’s unbanning, Zuma was elected Deputy Secretary General of the ANC. At the same time he was elected National Chairperson of the ANC, and in 1997 he became the organisation’s Deputy President.

title: Zuma, Jacob Gedleyihlekisa
content: Zuma was born in Zululand on 12 April 1942. Ø     Deputy President of the Republic of South Africa since 17 June 1999. Ø     Leader of government business in the National Assembly since June 1997. Ø     Deputy President of the African National Congress (ANC) since December 1997. Ø     Patron of the Jacob Zuma Bursary Fund (since 1998). Ø     Left South Africa in 1975 and for the next 12 years was based in Swaziland and later in Mozambique. During this period he was involved in underground work with President Mbeki and the others providing leadership to the ANC structures operating inside South Africa. Ø     Lived in several African countries working for the ANC and rose rapidly through the ranks to become a member of the National Executive Committee of the ANC in 1977. Ø     Elected National Chairperson of the ANC and Chairperson of the ANC in KZN. Ø     Honorary Doctorate of Administration from the University of Zululand (2001).

title: Jacob Gedleyihlekisa Zuma, Mr
content: Mr Jacob Gedleyihlekisa Zuma was the President of the Republic of South Africa from 9 May 2009 until 14 February 2018. After his release, President Zuma helped mobilise internal resistance and was instrumental in the re-establishment of ANC underground structures in the then Natal between 1974 and 1975. Following the unbanning of the ANC in February 1990, he was one of the first ANC leaders to return to South Africa to begin the process of negotiations with the then apartheid regime. In 1991, at the first ANC conference held in South Africa since 1959, he was elected Deputy Secretary General and after the 1994 elections, he requested to be deployed to KwaZulu Natal to work to cement peace between the ANC and Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP). He was elected ANC Deputy President in December 1997 and he served as Deputy President of the Republic of South Africa from 1999 until June 2005.
